questions.text: A partial data path of a processor is given in the figure, where [latex]RA[/latex], [latex]RB[/latex], and [latex]RZ[/latex] are 32-bit registers. Which option(s) is/are CORRECT related to arithmetic operations using the data path as shown?
questions.solution:
The given data path consists of:

- Two 32-bit registers: RA and RB.
- Two multiplexers (Mux_A and Mux_B).
- Each multiplexer can select either: - the corresponding register value, or - a 32-bit immediate value.
- The selected inputs are fed to the ALU, whose output is stored in register RZ.

Thus, the ALU can receive the following combinations of operands:

Mux_A Mux_B Operands
RA RB Two registers
RA Immediate One register + one immediate
Immediate RB One immediate + one register
Immediate Immediate Two immediate values

Now, evaluate each statement.

Option A: The data path can implement arithmetic operations involving two registers.

Since Mux_A can select RA and Mux_B can select RB, the ALU can perform operations such as [latex] RZ \leftarrow RA + RB [/latex]

Hence, Option A is Correct.

Option B: The data path can implement arithmetic operations involving one register and one immediate value.
Examples:
[latex] RZ \leftarrow RA + 10 [/latex] or [latex] RZ \leftarrow 20 + RB [/latex]
Therefore, Option B is Correct.

Option C: The data path can implement arithmetic operations involving two immediate values. Both multiplexers can independently select their immediate inputs. Therefore, the ALU can perform operations like [latex] RZ \leftarrow 15 + 25 [/latex]
Hence, Option C is Correct.

Option D: The data path can only implement arithmetic operations involving one register and one immediate value. This is false because the data path also supports:
- Register + Register
- Immediate + Immediate
- Register + Immediate

Therefore, Option D is Incorrect.

Click here for detail solution
options: The data path can implement arithmetic operations involving two registers.
The data path can implement arithmetic operations involving one register and one immediate value.
The data path can implement arithmetic operations involving two immediate values.
The data path can only implement arithmetic operations involving one register and one immediate value.

questions.text: Consider a digital display system (DDS) shown in the figure that displays the contents of register X. A 16-bit code word is used to load a word in X, either from S or from R. S is a 1024-word memory segment and R is a 32-word register file. Based on the value of mode bit M, T selects an input word to load in X. P and Q interface with the corresponding bits in the code word to choose the addressed word. Which one of the following represents the functionality of P, Q, and T?
questions.solution:
Match each block with its job:
- S has 1024 words, so the S-address is 10 bits. P must activate exactly one of 1024 words [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 10 : [latex]2^{10}[/latex] decoder.
- R has 32 words, so the R-address is 5 bits [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] Q is a 5 : [latex]2^5[/latex] decoder.
- T chooses one of two inputs (from S or R) using mode bit M [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 2 : 1 multiplexer.

Answer: P is 10:2^10 decoder; Q is 5:2^5 decoder; T is 2:1 multiplexer

questions.text:
Consider a main memory system that consists of 8 memory modules attached to the system
bus, which is one word wide. When a write request is made, the bus is occupied for 100
nanoseconds (ns) by the data, address, and control signals. During the same 100 ns, and for
500 ns thereafter, the addressed memory module executes one cycle accepting and storing the data. The (internal) operation of different memory modules may overlap in time, but only one request can be on the bus at any time. The maximum number of stores (of one word each) that can be initiated in 1 millisecond is ____________
questions.solution:
Each store holds the bus for 100 ns, and a module is busy for 600 ns. With 8 modules used in turn, a module is reused only after 8 [latex]\times[/latex] 100 = 800 ns [latex]\gt[/latex] 600 ns, so modules never cause waiting.

The bus is the bottleneck: one store per 100 ns.

[latex]\frac{1\,ms}{100\,ns}=\frac{10^{-3}}{10^{-7}}=10^4[/latex]

Answer: 10000
